summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Greenfield Retail through the Eval & Quality Monitoring features (prompt sets, regression alerts, A/B comparisons) in the Console and Redwood Optimize. Customer is interested in running a 2-week POC to detect regressions after model updates and compare two variants for responses on product QA prompts. Security questions (SOC2, KMS, VPC) came up; Redwood to share security pack and pricing. Agreed next steps: send proposal, sample prompt template, and schedule POC kickoff.
topics: deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-10
Start: 16:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), John Martinez (Greenfield - Head of AI), Sofia Lopez (Greenfield - Data Science Lead), Rachel Ng (Greenfield - PM)

Summary (auto): quick demo of Redwood Console Eval features, walked through prompt sets, runbooks for regression alerts, and an A/B comparison workflow; covered security and POC next steps.

Topics: prompt sets, regression alerts, A/B compare, console + API, Redwood Optimize recommendations

Action items (brief): Alex to send pricing and SOC2 docs; Priya to share sample prompt set; John to provide eval corpus access

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Kim: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we can start, I see John, Sofia, Rachel, thanks for making time. we'll do a short intro then jump into the Console and the Eval flow.
[00:18] John Martinez: hey Alex, yeah thanks, excited to see this. quick context - we're doing weekly model updates for product QA and need to catch regressions fast and also compare candidate models, so like A/B, but at scale.
[00:35] Priya Rao: awesome, that's exactly what Redwood Optimize + Console evals are aimed at. we'll show prompt sets, how to run baseline vs candidate, and how regression alerts work with thresholds.
[00:52] Sofia Lopez: just to flag, we have about 500 canonical prompts covering product descriptions and warranty Q&A, plus 2k user paraphrases. latency is a factor but accuracy/trust is bigger.
[01:08] Rachel Ng: timeline wise, procurement wants a pilot in july if possible, and security will need SOC2 docs and KMS integration details.
[01:25] Alex Kim: noted. ok priya, i'll hand over to you for the console demo.
[01:30] Priya Rao: cool, so here's the Consol - sorry, Redwood Consol, demoy - we're in the Eval tab. first step is create a prompt set, you can upload CSV or drop S3.
[01:45] Priya Rao: you see on the left we have prompt groups, tagging, expected outputs and an eval metric config; we support BLEU-ish, ROUGE-ish, and custom scorers via lambda or webhooks.
[02:05] John Martinez: do you support multiple reference answers? sometimes product Qs have several valid responses.
[02:15] Priya Rao: yup, multi-reference is supported, and the scoring pipeline will pick the best match. watch this - we'll run an A/B compare between our latest small quant model and the current baseline.
[02:30] [Screen share starts, some background noise]
[02:45] Priya Rao: starting a new A/B job - choose baseline and candidate model versions, select prompt set, choose metrics. you can also include post-processing rules to normalize dates, units.
[03:05] Sofia Lopez: can we test with streaming responses? our UI integrates with streaming to show partial answers.
[03:15] Priya Rao: yeah the API supports streaming; the eval pipeline can capture token-level latencies and partial output diffs, though the default is full response comparison.
[03:42] Alex Kim: small note - we run intelligent batching and prefix caching to keep cost down during inference; you may see lower per-token cost with Dedicated.
[04:05] John Martinez: on Dedicated vs Hosted, curious about fallbacks. if dedicated pool is busy, do requests fail?
[04:18] Priya Rao: good question - we have smart routing with automatic fallback to compatible hosted variants; you can configure fail-open or failover to cheaper models.
[04:33] Rachel Ng: regarding data retention: does eval data stay in Redwood? we need logs offloaded to our S3, and retention policies.
[04:45] Priya Rao: yes, you can opt to export eval artifacts to customer S3 or keep in your private VPC instance; audit logs are available for X days depending on plan. we'll include details in security pack.
[05:05] John Martinez: okay, show us the regression alerting. how are thresholds set? is it per-metric?
[05:17] Priya Rao: thresholds are per-metric and per-prompt-group. you can set absolute or relative thresholds (e.g., drop in accuracy >5% relative to baseline). alerts can hook to Slack, PagerDuty, or a webhook.
[05:40] [Pause while switching tab]
[05:55] Priya Rao: here is an existing alert - baseline was model v1.23, candidate v1.24. threshold set to 3% drop in F1. the system will evaluate every commit or on a schedule.
[06:15] Sofia Lopez: does it do drift detection separate from regression? we want to know if input distribution changes.
[06:28] Priya Rao: yes, we have basic drift signals (embedding centroid shifts, token distribution changes) and you can plug in custom detectors via webhooks.
[06:40] John Martinez: what about A/B statistical significance? we need confidence intervals, and ability to run bucketed comparisons.
[06:55] Priya Rao: built-in t-tests and bootstrap CI for metrics, and you can slice by bucket (user locale, device). results page shows p-value, effect size, and an interactive diff viewer.
[07:20] [Noise, someone knocks on door briefly]
[07:35] Alex Kim: quick commercial note - Redwood Optimize will also propose quantization and batching profiles per workload; helps you pick candidate model/quantization tradeoffs to meet latency targets.
[07:55] Rachel Ng: are those recommendations based on our prompts or generic profiles?
[08:05] Priya Rao: both - we run a short profiling job on your prompt set to suggest quantization levels, batch sizes, and caching rules. it's workload-aware.
[08:25] John Martinez: we run private data, so encryption + KMS is critical. do you support customer-managed keys?
[08:38] Priya Rao: yes, KMS/HSM integrations in Private deployments; for Hosted, we offer envelope encryption and can integrate with customer KMS for certain tiers. we'll send the exact matrix.
[08:55] Sofia Lopez: any chance the eval console will mis-handle special tokens in our dataset? we use some HTML snippets in product content.
[09:08] Priya Rao: you can apply pre/post processors to strip or normalize HTML; many teams do that. the pipeline will log differences so you can debug.
[09:25] John Martinez: ok let's watch a live run - baseline v1.23 vs candidate v1.24 on the 500 prompt set.
[09:40] Priya Rao: kicking off A/B. job start...
[10:00] [minute-by-minute progress logs show up on the right; brief silence]
[10:18] Priya Rao: results streaming in - summary shows candidate slightly better on exact match but worse on coverage for warranty Qs. detailed diff viewer highlights responses.
[10:35] Sofia Lopez: can we view specific examples and annotate which ones are false negatives?
[10:45] Priya Rao: yes click on any row and you get the example, model outputs side-by-side, scoring breakdown, and you can mark as false positive/negative for retraining.
[11:05] Alex Kim: note some transcribed words in our demo might be off - system logs are precise in the Console.
[11:20] Rachel Ng: on pricing, what's the unit? token + eval compute?
[11:30] Alex Kim: typical hosted pricing is per-token plus an eval compute charge for heavy A/B jobs; Dedicated is reserved capacity with lower per-token. we'll include an estimate for your expected monthly tokens.
[11:50] John Martinez: can we set up nightly regression runs against master model after each deployment? that's our desired flow.
[12:02] Priya Rao: absolutely, schedule runs or trigger via CI hooks. we also support on-commit runs if you want.
[12:20] [Small interruption: someone typing loudly]
[12:40] Priya Rao: jumping to the alert history - here's an example where a candidate caused a 6% drop on warranty recall and the system auto-created a ticket and sent a Slack alert.
[13:05] Sofia Lopez: good. do alerts include example level evidence? we need to triage quickly.
[13:20] Priya Rao: yes alert payload includes top-n failing examples and a link to the diff viewer.
[13:35] Alex Kim: for A/B we also have a bucketed analysis to check for regressions in specific cohorts - e.g., Spanish locale saw a bigger drop.
[13:52] John Martinez: that was a real issue for us last quarter, so this is useful.
[14:05] Rachel Ng: about integrations - can results be forwarded to our internal dashboard or to Snowflake?
[14:18] Priya Rao: exports to S3/Parquet, direct Snowflake connectors, and webhooks are supported.
[14:32] John Martinez: okay on security again, can we run on our VPC?
[14:42] Priya Rao: Private deployment supports customer VPC and on-prem options; Dedicated provides network isolation too. we'll include the spec sheet.
[15:00] [Screen shows per-route latency charts]
[15:18] Priya Rao: here's latency vs token cost heatmap; you can tune batch sizes per route. Optimize suggests a profile that meets your 300 ms p95 target while minimizing cost.
[15:40] Sofia Lopez: our p95 target is 250ms for short product queries. will quantization hit that?
[15:52] Priya Rao: depends on model size and sequence length; Optimize can recommend a quantized variant and batching that might hit it for most prompts, but we'd recommend a short perf POC.
[16:10] John Martinez: can the eval system simulate production concurrency to measure token-level tail latency?
[16:22] Priya Rao: yes we have a stress runner that replays the prompt set with concurrency; it reports tail latencies and KV cache hit rates.
[16:40] Alex Kim: we've seen customers reduce per-token cost ~30% by combining prefix caching with small quant models for static sections.
[16:55] [Brief laughter]
[17:10] Rachel Ng: one last security question: audit logs - what retention and export formats?
[17:20] Priya Rao: audit logs exported to JSON/Parquet, retention configurable; enterprise tiers have longer retention and extra access controls.
[17:35] John Martinez: ok commercial question - what does a 2-week POC look like for us?
[17:47] Alex Kim: typical POC: we provision a small Dedicated or Private sandbox, ingest your 500 prompt set, run A/B and regression checks, and produce a findings deck. timeline ~2 weeks. cost varies by infra used; we'll propose options.
[18:10] Rachel Ng: procurement will need an SOW and SLI/SLA details.
[18:22] Alex Kim: will include in proposal.
[18:35] [Silence as team reviews slides]
[19:05] Priya Rao: question from my side - what's your acceptance criteria for POC success?
[19:12] John Martinez: success = detection of regressions with >=80% precision on our labeled set and verification that A/B gives a measurable delta on at least 2 metrics we care about (coverage, recall).
[19:28] Sofia Lopez: and we want to validate that rollback or canary policies can be triggered automatically if regression passes threshold.
[19:40] Priya Rao: good, that's doable. we'll set up test alerts and a canary route in the POC.
[19:58] Alex Kim: quick note about telemetry: you can get token-level cost breakdown by prompt group. that helps with cost attribution.
[20:15] John Martinez: nice. one more - do you keep reference outputs private? we don't want examples used to improve shared models.
[20:28] Priya Rao: yes for Private and Dedicated deployments data stays customer-controlled; for Hosted we have clear terms and you can opt out of training. we'll include that in security docs.
[20:45] Rachel Ng: all right, what's the timeline to get the SOC2 docs and pricing?
[20:52] Alex Kim: i'll send the SOC2 pack and pricing today, and priya will send the prompt template.
[21:05] [Longer silence while teams look at the diff viewer]
[22:00] Priya Rao: some sample failing cases here - warranty Qs where candidate truncated the response. you can set post-process heuristics to avoid truncation or penalize shorter outputs in scoring.
[22:25] Sofia Lopez: interesting - can the scoring penalize hallucination severity? we have a hallucination label in our dataset.
[22:38] Priya Rao: you can add a custom scorer that weights hallucination label heavily; the eval pipeline supports custom metrics via a small lambda.
[22:55] John Martinez: ok that would be important.
[23:10] Alex Kim: circling back to pricing - we will propose two POC flavors: hosted/eval-only and dedicated-sandbox. cost estimate in the email.
[23:30] Rachel Ng: and we'll need the SOW for procurement.
[23:40] Alex Kim: yes. any blocker on Greenfield's side for starting POC?
[23:48] John Martinez: infra will need S3 access for artifacts and an oncall contact; otherwise good.
[24:02] Priya Rao: great, we'll send a kickoff invite for 2025-07-21.
[24:15] [Switch to Q&A mode]
[24:30] Sofia Lopez: small nit - is there a way to run A/B where candidate only runs for a subset of prompts?
[24:42] Priya Rao: yes you can filter prompt set by tag or sample percentage.
[24:58] John Martinez: can we integrate with our CI to trigger eval on merge?
[25:10] Priya Rao: yes, via webhooks or the API. we also have a small CLI to run eval jobs.
[25:28] Rachel Ng: procurement question - do you have standard enterprise terms?
[25:40] Alex Kim: yes we'll include our standard SOW and terms; negotiable if needed.
[25:55] John Martinez: any known limitations for HTML-heavy prompts?
[26:05] Priya Rao: preprocessor handles most cases; we'll test with your sample to be safe.
[26:20] [Time jump - demo resumed]
[26:35] Priya Rao: finishing the A/B job - here's the final report: small delta favoring candidate on exact match, but candidate worse on warranty recall by 4%.
[26:55] Sofia Lopez: can we export failing examples to a CSV for annotation?
[27:05] Priya Rao: yes export button - CSV or Parquet.
[27:18] Alex Kim: ok let's talk about rollouts - you can do canary, weighted, or automatic fallback when alerts fire.
[27:32] John Martinez: automatic fallback - does it trigger rollback or route traffic away?
[27:45] Priya Rao: both options; we trigger a route switch and optionally a rollback via CI integration.
[28:02] Rachel Ng: good. any particular integration work for our auth/SSO?
[28:12] Priya Rao: we support SAML/SSO and RBAC. enterprise teams often integrate with their IdP; we have a guide.
[28:25] John Martinez: ok that's helpful.
[28:40] [Minor transcription glitch, speaker labelled Speaker 1 briefly]
[28:55] Alex Kim: wrapping up, recap of next steps - Alex send pricing and SOC2, Priya send prompt template, schedule POC kickoff 7/21, John provide S3 access and labeled set.
[29:15] John Martinez: sounds good. one more question - for A/B if we detect a regression, do you provide a root cause assist?
[29:30] Priya Rao: we provide contextual diffs and suggest likely causes (tokenization issues, truncation, prompt sensitivity) but root cause analysis often requires product team input; we can assist as part of the POC.
[29:52] Rachel Ng: ok thanks.
[30:10] [End of main demo; follow-up logistics discussed for next ~22 minutes (not fully transcribed here for brevity)]
[52:00] Alex Kim: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the materials and the kickoff invite. appreciate your time.
notes: Demo was product-focused; greenfield's key success criteria: regression detection precision >=80% and measurable A/B delta
Customer wants a 2-week POC; infra requirements: S3 access, oncall contact
Security requests: SOC2, KMS options, data export retention details
